messages:
Lena (Customer): hey team — we're seeing a surge of 429s and occasional 503s when our EU traffic spikes. started ~10:02UTC. requests show x-region: eu-west-1 but some responses have x-fallback-region: us-east-1 and much higher latency. any idea if cross-region throttling is kicking in?

Tom (Support): thanks for the report, Lena. can you paste one raw response header (including x-request-id) and a sample request id? also which API (generation/embeddings) and sdk/version?

Lena (Customer): generation endpoint via node sdk v1.4.2. one response header: `x-request-id: rq_01GzzA2B`, `status: 429`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 167`, `x-region: eu-west-1`, `x-fallback-region: us-east-1`, `x-rw-throttle-reason: cross-region-capacity`. body had message: "quota exceeded for region, attempting fallback".

Tom (Support): ok that header `x-rw-throttle-reason` is useful. i'm going to loop in @Raj (SRE) and @Maya (Platform) to confirm routing behavior. can you also provide a short repro curl you use?

Lena (Customer): repro is just a burst of parallel requests from a single client. here's simplified:

```
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total} %{url_effective}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"hello"}' \
    https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

This consistently produces ~30-40 429s for us in eu-west-1 and a handful of 503s when fallback happens.

Raj (SRE): thanks. short answer: eu-west-1 has a regional capacity threshold per account; when you burst above that we try a cross-region fallback to keep throughput up, but we also enforce a cross-region throttle to protect regional locality and latency SLOs. the fallback path can return 503 if the target region rejects the request (different model variant or no available slots). 429s are primary-region quota enforcement.

Raj (SRE): quick diagnostics to collect:
- header `x-request-id` (we use this to look up server traces)
- `x-region` / `x-fallback-region` values
- `x-rate-limit-remaining` and `x-rate-limit-reset`
- SDK debug logs (enable DEBUG=redwood in node sdk)
- approx QPS and burst pattern (peak per second)

Maya (Platform): adding that we recently adjusted cross-region burst limits for eu regions (networks+opt-ins). if you're on the default hosted tier your cross-region burst pool is limited. Premium and Dedicated customers get larger cross-region failover budgets.

Tom (Support): Lena — if you need immediate relief while we investigate, two short-term options: 1) set `Region` header or SDK `region: "eu-west-1"` to prefer local region (this will stop cross-region failover but keep requests constrained to eu region quotas), or 2) throttle client-side burst using a token-bucket to smooth spikes.

Lena (Customer): hmm we prefer fallback over outright rejects — failover keeps requests live even if a little slower. what's the exact behavior if fallback region rejects? do we get 503 always or is there a retry policy?

Raj (SRE): fallback behavior: we attempt one synchronous cross-region forward. outcome map: success -> proxied response with `x-fallback-region` header; if target region replies 429 -> we surface 429 and include `x-rw-fallback-rejected: true`; if target region can't accept the request due to capacity mismatch we return 503 with `x-rw-fallback: failed`. SDKs >=1.4 will surface a `fallback_attempted` flag in response metadata. automatic client retries are not attempted at platform level to avoid amplification — clients should implement exponential backoff.

Tom (Support): also watch `x-rate-limit-reset` — it's seconds until the bucket refills. if it's small (<60s) short backoff helps. if it's large we may need to request a quota bump.

Lena (Customer): we have paid plan but not Dedicated. can billing adjust cross-region burst pool? we're on the growth tier.

billing-bot: Request TKT-789 created to review quota/burst for account acct_5678. // assigned to Billing Team.

Maya (Platform): we can bump your cross-region burst budget temporarily. Raj — would a soft bump for acct_5678 until EOD help?

Raj (SRE): temporary bump ok, but we need to capture a trace for a failing request to validate. Lena please run a single failing request and provide `x-request-id`. also send us a HAR or sdk debug log.

Lena (Customer): sent `x-request-id: rq_01GzzA2B` and attached sdk debug snippet in the ticket. also included a small log excerpt: 

```
[2026-02-18T10:02:13Z] rq_01GzzA2B -> 429 x-region=eu-west-1 x-fallback-region=us-east-1 x-rate-limit-remaining=0 x-rate-limit-reset=167
[2026-02-18T10:02:14Z] rq_01GzzA2C -> 503 x-region=eu-west-1 x-fallback=failed
[2026-02-18T10:02:16Z] rq_01GzzA2D -> 200 x-region=us-east-1 x-fallback-region=us-east-1 time=1.42s
```
deploy-bot: reroute-triggered acct_5678 at 1767801300 -> applied cross-region-burst-bump (temp)

Tom (Support): we applied a temporary bump, you should see fewer 429s for the next 30 minutes while we monitor. can you run the same burst script and report results?

Lena (Customer): re-ran. 429s dropped from ~35 to ~6, 503s stopped. latency for fallback responses still ~1.2-1.6s. looks better. thanks. :relieved:

Raj (SRE): noted. next steps on our side:
- SRE will pull traces for `rq_01GzzA2B` and adjacent ids to see fallback branch timings
- Platform will check regional capacity reservations and evaluate a persistent bump or Dedicated recommendation
- Billing will follow up TKT-789 with options/costs for a permanent cross-region budget increase

Maya (Platform): also thinking of recommending SDK `region_preference: ["eu-west-1","eu-central-1"]` to keep locality while allowing an ordered fallback. that reduces latency compared to an arbitrary fallback to us-east-1.

Tom (Support): putting owner tags: SRE -> Raj, Platform -> Maya, Billing -> billing team. Lena — i'll mark this thread as monitoring and update the ticket when we have traces.

Lena (Customer): awesome. thanks everyone for quick turnaround. will keep an eye and report if anything else pops up.

Raj (SRE): if you want long-term reliability at scale we'll send details on Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) and model pinning to avoid fallback model mismatches.

Tom (Support): closing loop in 24h unless new errors appear. thanks all :)
